name: MonarchDependencyPicker
title: DependencyPicker
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of relation headings and link rows (MonarchStatusGlyph, MonarchText, androidx.compose.foundation.clickable); MonarchSelect (androidx.compose.material3.ExposedDropdownMenuBox) for the relation and MonarchCombobox in its sheet presentation (androidx.compose.material3.ModalBottomSheet with a search field) to find the item
summary: Lists an item's links (blocked by, blocks, related to, duplicates, duplicated by) and adds new ones by choosing a relation and searching for the item in a sheet.
whenToUse: On an issue, task or ticket detail screen, to show and edit what blocks it, what it blocks, and related or duplicate items.
whenNotToUse: To pick one related record without a relation, use MonarchCombobox or MonarchEntityPicker. For a dependency graph across many items, use a timeline such as MonarchGanttTimeline.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDependencyPicker(value: List<MonarchDependencyLink>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onAdd: ((MonarchDependencyRelation, MonarchDependencyItem) -> Unit)? = null, onRemove: ((MonarchDependencyLink) -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((MonarchDependencyItem) -> Unit)? = null, items: List<MonarchDependencyItem> = emptyList(), excludeIds: Set<String> = emptySet(), relations: List<MonarchDependencyRelation> = MonarchDependencyRelation.entries, defaultRelation: MonarchDependencyRelation? = null, readOnly: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, query: String? = null, onQueryChange: ((String) -> Unit)? = null, removeIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchDependencyPickerLabels = MonarchDependencyPickerLabels())
enum class MonarchDependencyRelation { BlockedBy, Blocks, Relates, Duplicates, DuplicatedBy }
class MonarchDependencyItem(id: String, title: String, key: String? = null, status: MonarchStatusOption? = null)
class MonarchDependencyLink(id: String, relation: MonarchDependencyRelation, item: MonarchDependencyItem)

class MonarchDependencyPickerLabels(relations: Map<MonarchDependencyRelation, String> = emptyMap(), relationLabel: String? = null, searchLabel: String? = null, searchPlaceholder: String? = null, noResults: String? = null, empty: String? = null, remove: String? = null, removeItem: ((relation: String, item: String) -> String)? = null, added: ((relation: String, item: String) -> String)? = null, removed: ((relation: String, item: String) -> String)? = null, status: ((name: String) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The current links, shown grouped by relation in the order of relations.

options.name: onAdd
options.description: Asks the app to save a new link and update value. Without it there are no add controls.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Asks the app to remove a link. Without it rows have no remove button.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a linked item, for example its detail screen. Makes the row's text a button.

options.name: items
options.description: The items the search offers. Items already linked and excludeIds are left out.

options.name: excludeIds
options.description: Ids that cannot be linked, such as the item itself.

options.name: relations
options.description: The relations offered, in display order.

options.name: defaultRelation
options.description: The relation chosen at first; the first of relations when null.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Hides the add controls and the remove buttons.

options.name: enabled
options.description: When false the relation menu, the search and the remove buttons are disabled.

options.name: loading
options.description: Items are being fetched: the search sheet shows its loading state.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text, for a server search, with onQueryChange.

options.name: onQueryChange
options.description: Called with the search text on every keystroke. With it, every item in items is offered: the app filters on its server.

options.name: removeIcon
options.description: The icon of each remove button. Monarch bundles no icons; without it the buttons read "Remove".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the relation names.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No linked items." above the add controls.

states.name: links
states.description: A subheading per relation with links, then one row per link: the status glyph, the key in code style, the title and a remove button.

states.name: adding
states.description: The relation menu, then a search field that opens a bottom sheet with a search box and the matching items; picking one calls onAdd.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The menu, the search and the remove buttons are disabled.

appearance: Relation names use the subheading style, keys the code style in the muted text color, and titles the body style. The status glyph takes its category colors from MonarchStatusGlyph. Menus, the search sheet and buttons take their Monarch colors. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those roles.
platformNotes: The web searches in an inline combobox popover; on Android the search opens in a bottom sheet (MonarchCombobox's sheet presentation), the phone pattern for picking from a long list. The web links a title to an href; on Android onOpen makes the row a button and the app navigates, because components do not navigate. The web's onSearch with an AbortSignal is query and onQueryChange with app-side loading, as in MonarchCombobox. The web's headingLevel has no Android equivalent: headings are headings. Same name as iOS's plan; iOS has not built it yet.
accessibility: Each relation name is a heading, so a relation is never conveyed by position or color.
A row's glyph, key and title are read as one element, with the status by name ("Status: In progress"); with onOpen the element is a button with a 48dp touch target.
Remove buttons are named with the relation and the item ("Remove “Blocked by” link to STR-12 Fix the login redirect") and have 48dp touch targets.
Additions and removals are announced through a polite live region on an always-present node.
edgeCases: An item cannot be linked twice: linked items are left out of the search, whatever the relation.
Links whose relation is not in relations are not shown.
The app decides whether a reverse link (blocks / blocked by) is created on the other item.
Long titles wrap; keys stay on one line.

examples.title: Issue dependencies
examples.template:
MonarchDependencyPicker(
    value = links,
    onAdd = { relation, item -> links = links + MonarchDependencyLink("${relation.name}-${item.id}", relation, item) },
    onRemove = { link -> links = links - link },
    items = items,
    excludeIds = setOf({{excludeIds.0}}),
)
examples.code:
MonarchDependencyPicker(
    value = links,
    onAdd = { relation, item -> links = links + MonarchDependencyLink("${relation.name}-${item.id}", relation, item) },
    onRemove = { link -> links = links - link },
    items = items,
    excludeIds = setOf("12"),
)

examples.title: Read only, with status
examples.code:
MonarchDependencyPicker(
    value = listOf(
        MonarchDependencyLink(
            id = "l1",
            relation = MonarchDependencyRelation.BlockedBy,
            item = MonarchDependencyItem(
                id = "12",
                title = "Fix the login redirect",
                key = "STR-12",
                status = MonarchStatusOption("doing", "In progress", MonarchStatusCategory.Started),
            ),
        ),
    ),
    readOnly = true,
)
